title: Viniyoga of imaṃ me varuṇa

words.role: first word of the first mantra quoted
first word of the second mantra quoted

words.meaning: thus; marks the words before it as a quotation

words.gram: compound, n. loc. sg. (M’s spelling of सन्ध्योपस्थाने)

words.role: what the mantra is used for

sandhi.rule: a final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra

translation.literal: Of the mantras “imaṃ me” and “tat tvā yāmi”: Śunaḥśepa the seer, gāyatrī and triṣṭubh the metres, Varuṇa the deity, the use in the evening sandhyā upasthāna.
translation.readable: Imaṃ me varuṇa and tat tvā yāmi: seer Śunaḥśepa, metres gāyatrī and triṣṭubh, deity Varuṇa; used for the evening upasthāna.

sandhi_exceptions.note: The prayoga leaves two vowels side by side across a phrase boundary of the formula, without joining them.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: the evening upasthāna to Varuṇa, imaṃ me varuṇa and tat tvā yāmi (TS 2.1.11.6; RV 1.25.19, 1.24.11), followed by yac cid dhi te and two more ṛks. Śunaḥśepa is the seer named; the first verse is a gāyatrī, the second a triṣṭubh. The commas of the witness mark the pauses between the parts; a word before a comma keeps its pausal form.
in_the_rite: Evening service, step surya-upasthana, before imaṃ me varuṇa (M only).

flags.text: M writes सन्ध्योपस्थाने for सन्ध्योपस्थाने. A correction should be considered.
